catalog_quote: [p.1, abstract] Kunama has been reported by different scholars as having two or three tones, downstep (or not), contrastive length of both consonants and vowels, and lexical stress. ... we present phonological and phonetic evidence for the existence of three level tones ... No evidence for lexical stress is found. [pp.2-3] ... Tucker and Bryan [1966] ... observe that "[t]one and stress appear to be significant, both lexically and grammatically." [1966: 337]. ... [Thompson] was of the opinion that there was a correlation between vowel length and stress [1983: 284]. ... Elsewhere stress is reported as usually occurring on syllables preceding geminates [1983: 283]. These statements would appear to suggest an accentual assignment that was sensitive to syllable weight. ...
